title: Rolling-slate orchestration and critical-skill escrow procedure
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Create a repeatable operational procedure for rolling-slate cycle orchestration that preserves delivery momentum while protecting a small, fast-moving pool of critical skills (the 'skill escrow'). This playbook covers how PMs, ENG, and Design coordinate fractional staffing, role-shadowing, and emergency escrow activation during mid-cycle surges or cross-initiative interruptions. The goal is to reduce mid-cycle context switching costs, improve predictability for high-impact launches, and formalize on-call-style stewardship for mission-critical roles.
acceptance_criteria: Procedure documented in Confluence with step-by-step roles/responsibilities
Escrow pool size and activation thresholds defined and agreed by Eng and PM leadership
Decision matrix for scope-trimming and surge activation validated in tabletop run with three engineering teams
Rollout communication template created for engineering managers and product leads
Dashboards added to Console to surface skill-escrow utilization and cycle drift metrics
tasks: Draft procedure and decision matrix (owner: PM)
Workshop with Eng leads to define skill categories and minimum escrow sizing (owner: ENG lead)
Design communication templates and role shadowing checklist (owner: Design)
Implement telemetry signals for escrow activation and cycle drift (owner: Observability team)
Run tabletop scenario with three squads and capture runbook gaps (owner: PM)
Finalize Confluence playbook and obtain sign-off from GTM and Eng leadership (owner: PM)
Publish to team channels and schedule 30-min sync for Q&A (owner: PM)
Add label mappings in Linear to tag escrow activations for retrospective analysis (owner: Growth Ops)

2026-03-02 Miguel Santos: Proposed escrow sizing = 10% of rostered engineers on initiative-critical teams, min 1 senior/1 mid per pillar. Need Eng leadership buy-in.
2026-03-03 Priya Shah (ENG): Concern that a hard 10% may starve feature work; propose a flexible band 6-12% with SLA-backed priority windows.
2026-03-04 Design review (Liam Chen): Role-shadowing checklist updated to include handover template and UI/Console access pre-checks.
2026-03-05 Ops note (Dana Ruiz): Observability will expose two signals: escrow_utilization_pct and cycle_velocity_delta. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/observability/pull/482
2026-03-05 PM update: Tabletop scheduled for 2026-03-18 with runtime, console, and dedicated capacity squads. Action items assigned in tasks list.
decision_log: 2026-03-03 Decision: Adopt flexible escrow band (6-12%) instead of fixed 10% to balance risk and throughput
2026-03-04 Decision: Escrow activation requires approval by Eng lead + PM for the initiative unless emergency override declared by VP Eng
2026-03-05 Decision: Skill categories = Runtime Core, Serving Infra, Observability, Console UX, Security/CICD. Escrow must include at least two categories for cross-functional resilience
risks: Overcommitting senior engineers to escrow may delay longer-term roadmap milestones
Poorly defined activation thresholds could lead to unnecessary context switches
Insufficient telemetry will make retrospective sizing decisions noisy
Adoption resistance from teams that prefer first-come staffing for hot projects
notes: Example activation scenario included: runtime-1.18 hotfix conflicts with console feature freeze; escrow used to frontload runtime patching for 72 hours while feature work is paused
We will track two primary metrics: escrow_utilization_pct (target < 70% during non-emergency) and cycle_velocity_delta (target < 15% drop during escrow activation)
Playbook must include sample scope-cut templates: (A) defer non-blocking UI polish, (B) reduce integration tests scope for canary, (C) soft freeze with documented rollback plan
Future iteration: tie escrow activation to Dedicated capacity signal when GPU availability drops below 80% for key regions
If tabletop surfaces >3 gaps, appointment of a rotating Escrow Steward role for the next cycle will be proposed
